slides: Welcome back, and now the range chart. A range is everything from the smallest value to the biggest one.
The exam loves the smallest and the biggest possible values, in every topic. In charts too.

slides.say: This chart shows a survey of the monthly rent of flats in Tel Aviv in two thousand twelve, by the number of rooms.
Across the bottom, the number of rooms. Going up, the rent, in thousands of shekels.
Look at the bottom of the axis. There's a Z. Remember, it tells us that from zero to two is not to scale.
Each bar here is a range. The bottom of a bar is the lowest rent for that number of rooms.
The top of the bar is the highest rent.
And the bold line inside the bar is the mean rent, the average.
The example says, in six-room flats the lowest rent was four thousand five hundred. The highest was eight thousand, and the mean was six thousand five hundred.

slides: And on the chart, the six-room bar goes from four and a half to eight, with the bold line at six and a half. It matches.

slides.say: Is the mean always in the middle of the bar? No. Look at two rooms.
It goes from two thousand five hundred to four thousand five hundred. The middle of that is three thousand five hundred.
But the mean is four thousand, higher than the middle. Why?
at: But the mean is four thousand

slides.say: Say there's just one cheap flat, at two thousand five hundred. All the other flats cost four thousand or more. The many dear flats pull the mean up.
So the bar shows where the rents start and end. The bold line shows the average. They're different things.
Here's a sample question. Ella rents a two-room flat, and she rents out a five-room flat.
Daniel rents a one-room flat, and he rents out a four-room flat.
Each one saves the difference between the two rents every month. Which of these cannot be the difference between their savings?
First, what's the difference between rent and rent out? Ella owns the five-room flat. She rents it out, so she gets the money.
And she lives in the two-room flat. She rents it, so she pays. So her saving is what she gets, minus what she pays.
What's the most Ella can save? She gets the most, and she pays the least. The most for five rooms is seven thousand five hundred.
The least for two rooms is two thousand five hundred. Seven thousand five hundred minus two thousand five hundred is five thousand.
And the least she can save? She gets the least, four thousand five hundred. And she pays the most, also four thousand five hundred.
Four thousand five hundred minus four thousand five hundred is zero. So Ella saves anywhere from zero to five thousand.
at: minus four thousand five hundred is zero

slides.say: Now Daniel, the same way. The most he can save: he gets the most for four rooms, seven thousand. He pays the least for one room, two thousand.
at: he gets the most for four rooms

slides.say: Seven thousand minus two thousand is five thousand.
The least: he gets four thousand, and he pays the most for one room, also four thousand. That's zero.
So each one saves something from zero to five thousand.
Now the question. Can the difference between them be zero? Yes, if they both save the same amount.

slides: Two thousand five hundred? Yes, for example five thousand and two thousand five hundred. Five thousand? Yes, if one saves five thousand and the other saves zero.

slides.say: And five thousand five hundred? The biggest difference is when one saves the most and the other saves the least. Five thousand minus zero is only five thousand.
So five thousand five hundred is impossible. That's choice number four.
The same data can also come as a table. Then each cell has three numbers, and the place of each number tells its meaning.

slides: The note says, top left is the lowest rent, the centre is the mean, and bottom right is the highest.

slides.say: So one room: the lowest is two, the mean is three, and the highest is four, in thousands. Just like the bar.
Four rooms: the lowest is four, the mean is five and a half, and the highest is seven.

slides: Tables like this, with two or three numbers in a cell, are common on the exam. So always read the note.

slides.say: Which is better? In a table, it's easy to add more cities. Each city is one more row.
In a chart, three cities make three bars for each number of rooms. It gets busy.
But it's easy to compare. We see right away which city has higher bars.
